gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 'Plex hardware transcoding' column means three different things. The UGREEN DXP8800 Plus transcodes on its built-in Quick Sync graphics, but only with Plex in Docker plus Plex Pass. The QNAP TS-873A can transcode only with a bus-powered graphics card such as a GTX 1650 in one of its two PCIe slots, and QNAP says that GPU stops transcoding for QTS while Virtualization Station is using it. The Synology DS1825+ has no graphics-card path at all: its one PCIe slot (x4 link) lists only network cards, so adding 10GbE (E10G30-T1, one RJ45 port) uses the only slot.
standout_why: Compared against the cited pages: WunderTech's best 8-bay article says not to buy the TS-873A or DS1825+ for Plex but never mentions graphics cards or what the DS1825+ slot accepts. ComputingForGeeks lists TS-873A transcoding as 'not stated' and gives maker power figures without their test conditions. StarryHope's Plex article covers neither model. The QNAP hardware-spec page ChatGPT cited lists the PCIe slots but not the GTX 1650 support or its caveat. Two ChatGPT answers guessed 'Add-on GPU required' or 'Optional GPU' for the TS-873A, but no source they got backs it, and none says the DS1825+ slot has no GPU path or that its single slot is the only route to 10GbE. Our own current page marks both AMD boxes simply 'No hardware transcoding'.
decides: Confirms the DXP8800 Plus as the pick for running Plex or Jellyfin on the NAS: it is the only candidate that transcodes out of the box and also has 2× 10GbE built in. It changes how the QNAP should be presented: the TS-873A can transcode, but only by giving one of its two PCIe slots to a graphics card, so a GPU plus 10GbE uses both slots. The DS1825+ stays a storage-only or direct-play pick: its single slot can hold a 10GbE card or nothing else, and no graphics card is listed for it.

findings.label: Hardware transcoding path
findings.value: Only with a bus-powered graphics card in a PCIe Gen3 x4 slot (QNAP names the NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650). QNAP: when Virtualization Station uses the card, 'the NAS will temporarily stop hardware transcoding acceleration for QTS'.
findings.note: The product page says the PCIe slots 'support high-profile graphics cards that do not need power cables, including NVIDIA GeForce GTX1650' and lists 4K UHD transcoding as a use. It has 2 slots in total, and 10GbE also needs a card (QM2 or a NIC), so a GPU plus 10GbE fills both.

findings.label: Expansion slots / built-in LAN
findings.value: 2× PCIe Gen3 x4 (high-profile cards); 2× 2.5GbE built in; 10GbE only via an add-in card
findings.note: The page offers the QM2 M.2+10GbE card or a 5GbE/10GbE NIC.

findings.label: PCIe slot and what it accepts
findings.value: 1× Gen3 x8 slot (x4 link); listed cards: E25G30-F2, E10G30-T2, E10G30-T1, E10G30-F2 (network cards only, no GPU)
findings.note: There is one slot, so 10GbE (or 25GbE) uses it and nothing else can be added. The built-in LAN is 2× 2.5GbE RJ45.

findings.label: 10GbE card needed to match built-in 10GbE
findings.value: E10G30-T1: 1× 10GbE RJ45, PCIe 3.0 x4, low-profile and full-height brackets; DS1825+ is on its applied-models list
findings.note: Even with this card the DS1825+ gets one 10GbE port, against two built into the DXP8800 Plus.

findings.label: Rated power (maker)
findings.note: The spec page gives no drive count or drive model and links to a Knowledge Center method article whose body would not render (see unsourced). Not comparable to QNAP's or UGREEN's figures without that method.

findings.label: Rated noise (maker)
findings.note: Synology's conditions: fully installed with Synology SATA HDDs, idle, two GRAS 40AE microphones 1 m from the front and rear, background 16.49–17.51 dB(A). Idle only, so not a load figure.

findings.label: Max memory / warranty
findings.value: 32 GB (2× 16 GB); 8 GB DDR4 ECC pre-installed; 3-year warranty, 5 with Extended Warranty Plus (Europe and North America only)
findings.note: Synology says it 'will not provide complete product warranty or technical support' when non-Synology memory is added.

findings.label: Rated power (maker)
findings.note: QNAP's footnote says 'Tested with drives fully populated' but names no drive model. It gives no noise figure. PSU 250 W. Max memory 64 GB (2× 32 GB). Warranty 3 years.
